title: Draw a trajectory to show the pace of change along a path.
rule: Use a trajectory or speed chart, a reference form, to show how fast something moved along a path: dots at equal time steps along a connected path, so wide spacing means fast change and close spacing slow. Mark the start and end and name the steps.
use_when: A specialist asks not only where two measures went but how fast they got there.

use_instead.when: The relationship over time, without the pace
One measure’s rate of change over time

text: Equal time steps turn the spacing of the dots into speed, which a plain path hides. The reader sees where change raced and where it stalled.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: No kit form: draw a trajectory from connected-scatter with dots at equal time steps.
sketch_alt: A curved path with dots at equal time steps, spaced wide where change ran fast and close together where it slowed, from a start dot to an end dot.
